newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Benpres 1996 net seen up 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Benpres 1996 net seen up 25 pct.

text.p: Diversified firm Benpres Holdings Corp is expected to rely on its traditional businesses in broadcasting, banking and power to steer 1996 profits to its targeted growth level of 25 percent, brokers said on Wednesday.
A Reuters poll of eight brokerage houses completed this week showed that Benpres was expected to report 2.02 billion pesos in net profits for 1996, up from 1.616 billion pesos in 1995.
The analysts expected 1997 profits to rise by a further 25 percent to 2.54 billion pesos.
"Growth in earnings for 1996 will be driven by its traditional businesses namely ABS-CBN, PCIBank and First Philippine Holdings," ING Barings analyst Gio de la Rosa said.
But for 1997, profits growth was seen coming from its telecommunications unit ICC Telecoms and property development arm Rockwell Land Corp, they said.
"ABS-CBN remains Benpres' biggest source of earnings", Guoco Securities analyst Saturnino Mejia said.
Benpres, controlled by the Lopez family, owns 71 percent of the country's television market and is expected to corner a big chunk of the industry's advertising receipts.
Benpres may also expect Sky Vision Corp, the largest provider of cable television services in the country, to propel earnings up, analysts added. Benpres has a 20 percent stake in Sky Vision.

A steady flow of earnings may also be expected from First Philippine Holdings Corp, which is 26.59 percent owned by Benpres and is the largest stockholder of Manila Electric Co (Meralco) with a 14 percent equity interest.

Benpres itself has a 1.72 percent stake in Meralco, the country's biggest power distributor, which recently announced that 1996 sales volume rose by 12.2 percent, exceeding its 8 to 10 percent growth sales projection for the year.
Michael Licaros, analyst at Citisecurities Inc, said Benpres' profits will be boosted by an expected 15 percent earnings growth of PCIBank, a universal bank, where it has a 17.74 percent stake.
In 1997, Rockwell Land Corp and ICC Telecoms are expected to start contributing to Benpres' profits.
"Among the local carriers, ICC Telecoms is ahead in installing (phone) lines while Rockwell had already pre-sold units," Helen Alvarez, research head at All Asia Securities Inc, said.
Benpres, along with Lyonnaise des Eaux SA, has submitted a bid for the privatisation of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS), the country's biggest water utility.

If it wins the contract, it would mean a cash outflow for Benpres in 1997 as the winning bidders are expected to invest in infrastructure to upgrade the leaky waterworks system, Erwin Tan, research head at Abacus Securities Corp, said.
